fieldMarks: Tall, all-gray crane with a red patch on the head.
Bushy tuft of feathers over the rump; bill smaller than a great blue heron's.
behavior: Elaborate dancing courtship with wing-spreading and leaping.
Omnivorous: insects, roots, rodents, snails, frogs, berries, seeds and waste grain; forages in flocks outside breeding season.
Northern populations migrate long distances in flocks and formations; Florida, Mississippi and Cuban populations are resident.
habitat: Prairies, fields, marshes and tundra; breeds in open freshwater wetlands and shallow marshes.
range: Breeds from Alaska and northern and western Canada through the northern and western US and Great Lakes; resident populations in Florida and Mississippi; some birds cross the Bering Strait.

lookalikes.name: Great blue heron
lookalikes.howToTell: The crane has a smaller bill, a red crown and a bushy rump 'bustle'.
